newsitem.title: UK: Option volume stifles gold market moves - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Option volume stifles gold market moves - analyst.

text.p: The vast increase in bullion options business was a key factor behind the underlying gold market's current very low volatility, a metal market analyst said on Wednesday.
As much as 10 to 15 million ounces of physical gold could be committed currently to the over-the-counter (OTC) market, according to Merrill Lynch market analyst Ted Arnold.
"The great bulk of this gold is being granted to the bullion market by central banks and producers and these are players who do not mind being called away on their options," Arnold said.
The high-low range of the London gold fix during August of $3.00 was the smallest in 20 years, he said.
"Option volatilities have been close to record lows in recent weeks but this is probably because grantors are selling more and more options," Arnold said.
Official Comex figures for end September show the exchange's option volumes are over 15 percent higher than they were last year at a record 1.68 million lots.
Analysts estimated the still-growing OTC volume to be about two-thirds larger than that on Comex.
Arnold said the deadening impact on the underlying market's volatility came from options strangles using puts and calls around the current price.

While the option grantor (like central banks and miners) did not need to hedge, the option holders did. But selling into strength against calls and buying into weakness against their puts, effectively stifled any price momentum. "(The option writers) are still making money if they have gold in their vaults valued at $250 an ounce or gold in the ground at say $300 an ounce cost of production," Arnold said.
"Our research also suggests that the strikes do not really fall away in volume until you are below $370 or above $420," he added.
